title: Dependency Injection Best Practices knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Dependency Injection Best Practices”?
options: Dependency Injection Best Practices helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Dependency Injection Best Practices means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Dependency Injection Best Practices removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Dependency Injection Best Practices should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Dependency Injection Best Practices helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Dependency Injection Best Practices is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Explicit service responsibilities” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Explicit service responsibilities” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Explicit service responsibilities” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Explicit service responsibilities” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Explicit service responsibilities” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Explicit service responsibilities” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Explicit service responsibilities” under Dependency Injection Best Practices. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Dependency Injection Best Practices”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
